name: Isolated Splenic Vein Thrombosis

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of thrombosis localized to the splenic vein without involvement of the portal or superior mesenteric veins
Presence of isolated gastric varices or left-sided portal hypertension symptoms without generalized portal hypertension
Exclusion of portal vein thrombosis or systemic causes of portal hypertension
Laboratory evidence of hypercoagulable state or underlying pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic confirmation of isolated splenic vein thrombosis plus clinical evidence of left-sided portal hypertension with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical correlation; no universally accepted formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in the fundus of the stomach
Due to splenic vein obstruction causing localized portal hypertension
searchTerms: high blood pressure in left portal vein
increased pressure in splenic vein area

common.notes: Enlargement of the spleen due to venous congestion

common.symptomName: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding from gastric varices
common.notes: May present as hematemesis or melena
Often related to splenic infarction or congestion

occasional.notes: Secondary to chronic blood loss or hypersplenism
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.notes: Due to splenomegaly or gastric varices
May cause localized pain and tenderness

rare.notes: Rare progression beyond isolated splenic vein
Rare but possible in advanced cases

laboratory: Mild thrombocytopenia due to splenic sequestration
Possible elevated D-dimer if acute thrombosis
Normal liver function tests (distinguishes from generalized portal hypertension)
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing absence of flow in splenic vein
Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI demonstrating splenic vein thrombosis without portal vein involvement
Splenomegaly and gastric varices on imaging
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; evaluation for thrombophilia may be indicated
other: Endoscopy revealing isolated gastric varices without esophageal varices

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of portal vein on imaging
Generalized portal hypertension with esophageal varices
Diffuse liver parenchymal disease on imaging
Elevated liver enzymes and synthetic dysfunction
Presence of both esophageal and gastric varices
Mass lesion in pancreas on imaging
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss

redFlags: Massive upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage from ruptured gastric varices
Rapidly enlarging splenomegaly with severe abdominal pain
Extension of thrombosis into portal or mesenteric veins
references: Sarin SK, et al. Portal vein thrombosis: clinical features and management. J Hepatol. 2020.
Kumar S, et al. Isolated splenic vein thrombosis: a review of clinical features and management. World J Gastroenterol. 2019.
Orphanet: Isolated splenic vein thrombosis. ORPHA:583856.
